issue_comments.body: Might I ask why the longer spelling should be the preferred one?

I think being more precise about things being about the identity is better than it being about `1` which has the possibility of being misinterpreted as a different `1` than the identity. For example, there's [LinearMap.convOne_def](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/RingTheory/Coalgebra/Convolution.html#LinearMap.convOne_def) which is not the identity.

There are hundreds of `One` instances throughout Mathlib. I don't believe that this possibility of misinterpretation is something we care much about, particularly when we have the typechecker to help out.

The fact that `ContinuousLinearMap` is (under suitable assumptions) a `Semiring` or even a `Ring` is to me very clear evidence that we should prefer the `1` spelling. That way we get all of the usual boilerplate (`mul_one`, `one_mul`, etc.) for free.

> The fact that ContinuousLinearMap is (under suitable assumptions) a Semiring or even a Ring is to me very clear evidence that we should prefer the 1 spelling.

That's my point though. There are other rings than the typical one (under the right assumptions). The `1` we use is the identity, not just for any ring.

I feel like newcomers who scroll through the documentation would get confused. Sometimes I get confused for a moment when I'm scrolling through various documentation.

@vihdzp, alright I reverted all of the changes you didn't like. Now this just changes `smulRight (1 : R →L[R] R)` to `toSpanSingleton` and adds the appropriate API.

The other change is bigger and clearly needs more discussion :).

timeline.body: Might I ask why the longer spelling should be the preferred one?

I think being more precise about things being about the identity is better than it being about `1` which has the possibility of being misinterpreted as a different `1` than the identity. For example, there's [LinearMap.convOne_def](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/RingTheory/Coalgebra/Convolution.html#LinearMap.convOne_def) which is not the identity.

There are hundreds of `One` instances throughout Mathlib. I don't believe that this possibility of misinterpretation is something we care much about, particularly when we have the typechecker to help out.

The fact that `ContinuousLinearMap` is (under suitable assumptions) a `Semiring` or even a `Ring` is to me very clear evidence that we should prefer the `1` spelling. That way we get all of the usual boilerplate (`mul_one`, `one_mul`, etc.) for free.

> The fact that ContinuousLinearMap is (under suitable assumptions) a Semiring or even a Ring is to me very clear evidence that we should prefer the 1 spelling.

That's my point though. There are other rings than the typical one (under the right assumptions). The `1` we use is the identity, not just for any ring.

I feel like newcomers who scroll through the documentation would get confused. Sometimes I get confused for a moment when I'm scrolling through various documentation.
